analysis: The PR only changes documentation: docs/developer/test.md (head lines 923-935) adds a paragraph on FlintOpenRouterLiveTests and FlintRelayLogprobsLiveTests, and docs/provider/direct-mode.md (head lines 183-189) adds Flint reasoning-control semantics. No executable code, auth, attestation, encryption, key handling, or cache logic is changed, so no control or trust boundary (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011) is altered. The test docs keep the live tests opt-in (DARKBLOOM_FLINT_OPENROUTER_LIVE=1, loopback HTTP, an owned cache). Nothing points them at production or at a live provider's state. The sealed relay logprobs test goes through the production handler and its stated purpose is checking entries. T-008 (fail-closed encryption) is not weakened by this text. The direct-mode text says reasoning.exclude, include_reasoning:false and reasoning.enabled:false omit reasoning from the response while its tokens are still counted. That is a response-shaping behavior, not a data-exposure change. It does not establish how the described behavior is implemented, and the corresponding code is not in this PR. T-041 prefix-cache properties (HMAC names, 30-minute TTL, account scoping) are not touched by the new text. Remaining integration question: the doc claims about Flint reasoning omission and logprobs behavior depend on the SDK and provider code, which was not supplied here, so those claims are unverified. They are documentation claims only and carry no security-relevant regression evidence.
